name: Elevance Health
tagline: Bringing together the concepts of elevate and advance
hero_kpi_rationale: Le nombre d'adhérents médicaux est la mesure d'échelle clé d'un assureur santé. Il pilote les primes encaissées et reflète la position concurrentielle d'Elevance, premier assureur des États-Unis en nombre de membres.

kpis.signal: Adhésions médicales en baisse de 1,1 % en 2025, sous l'effet de l'attrition Medicaid après la fin des dispositions d'urgence sanitaire.
kpis.description: Nombre total d'adhérents médicaux au 31 décembre (en millions). Elevance sert environ 45,2 millions de membres, restant le premier assureur santé des États-Unis par le nombre de membres.

kpis.signal: Ratio de charges de prestations à 90,0 % en 2025, +150 points de base, sous pression d'une hausse des coûts médicaux sur toutes les lignes.
kpis.description: Charges de prestations rapportées aux primes encaissées (Benefit expense ratio). À 90,0 % en 2025, en hausse de 150 points de base, reflet de la tendance haussière des coûts médicaux du segment Health Benefits.

kpis.signal: Revenu Carelon Services en bond de 58 % en 2025, moteur de diversification au-delà de l'assurance santé.
kpis.description: Chiffre d'affaires opérationnel du segment Carelon Services (services de santé, gestion des soins). À 28 316 M$ en 2025, principal relais de croissance d'Elevance hors assurance.
kpis._source: SEC 10-K ELV FY2025 (Reportable segments operating revenue)

kpis.signal: Revenu du segment assurance Health Benefits en hausse de 11 % en 2025, premier segment d'Elevance.
kpis.description: Chiffre d'affaires opérationnel du segment Health Benefits (assurance santé). Premier segment du groupe, à 167 094 M$ en 2025.
kpis._source: SEC 10-K ELV FY2025 (Reportable segments operating revenue)

kpis.signal: Adhésions Medicaid en chute depuis 2022, conséquence de la fin des inscriptions automatiques liées à l'urgence sanitaire.
kpis.description: Nombre d'adhérents Medicaid au 31 décembre (en millions). En recul à 8,5 millions en 2025 contre un pic de 11,6 millions en 2022, du fait de l'attrition post-pandémie.
kpis._source: SEC 10-K ELV FY2025 (Medical membership by customer type)

risks.title: Healthcare Cost Management
risks.score_rationale: Healthcare costs are critical to profitability. The 10-K explicitly states that numerous factors affecting healthcare costs may adversely affect the company's ability to predict and manage such costs, including changes in healthcare practices, utilization patterns, demographic characteristics, medical cost inflation, and increased labor costs. This directly impacts the company's cash flows and financial condition. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is exposed to risks related to healthcare cost management. Failure to appropriately predict and price for healthcare costs could adversely affect profitability and financial results.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: As a health insurer handling sensitive member data, the company faces material cybersecurity risks. Data breaches could compromise member privacy, result in regulatory penalties, and damage reputation, all of which could negatively impact operations and financial condition. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks that could compromise sensitive member data and result in operational and financial losses.

risks.title: Regulatory and Compliance Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company operates under strict healthcare regulations including data protection and privacy requirements. Regulatory changes could increase operational costs and complexity. The 10-K mentions the company's compliance with applicable regulations and the potential for regulatory changes to impact operations. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is subject to strict healthcare and data protection regulations that could change and increase operational burden.

risks.title: Competitive Pressure
risks.score_rationale: The health insurance market is competitive, with customers able to switch providers based on pricing and service quality. The company must maintain competitive advantage through differentiated offerings and operational efficiency. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company operates in a competitive market where pricing and service quality are key differentiators for customer retention.

risks.title: Government Program Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company generates significant revenue from government programs including Medicaid and Medicare. Changes in government reimbursement rates or program policies could materially impact revenue and profitability. (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is exposed to risks from dependence on government programs, where policy changes could negatively impact financial results.

company_description: Elevance Health, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a health benefits company in the United States. The company operates in four segments: Health Benefits, CarelonRx, Carelon Services, and Corporate & Other. It offers a variety of health plans and services to individual, employer group risk-based and fee-based, BlueCard, Medicare, Medicaid, and FEP members; health products; a broad array of fee-based administrative managed care services; and specialty and other insurance products and services, such as stop loss, dental, vision, and supplemental health insurance benefits. The company also operates in the pharmacy services business; and markets and offers pharmacy services, including home delivery and specialty pharmacies, claims adjudication, formulary management, pharmacy networks, rebate administration, a prescription drug database, and member services, as well as infusion services and injectable therapies through ambulatory infusion centers. In addition, it provides healthcare related services and capabilities, including specialty care enablement and utilization management support for specialized clinical domains; behavioral health and comprehensive care management
